Title: What are acceptable punishments for misbehavior during tournament?

Messages.Author: Satrapa
Messages.Body:
What are acceptable punishments for misbehavior during tournament?
What would be acceptable for stalling, cheating or smoking (when law
don't prohibit it but organizer asked not to smoke).

Messages.Author: Petri Wessman
Messages.Body:


Well, if/when I'm running a tournament

- clear stalling gets a warning, multiple warnings will result in a
disqualification
- cheating (clear and provable) gets an immediate disqualification.
With a more murky case I'd probably go with just a warning, it
depends.
- smokers would be asked (forcefully) to stop at once, if they don't,
well... I'd kick them out. Players have to abide by the rules set by
the venue/organizer.

I've been blessed with very pleasant and sportsmanlike (or fiendishly
clever ;) players over the years though, I think I've only given out
one warning or something like that.

-Petri

Messages.Author: John Whelan
Messages.Body:
On Mar 9, 10:25 am, Satrapa <jedrzej.komorow...@gmail.com> wrote:
> What are acceptable punishments for misbehavior during tournament?

Acceptable:
-- A "caution";
-- A "warning";
-- A game loss;
-- A disqualification.

Unacceptable:
-- Judge gets to keep your cards
-- Forfeiture of First-born Child
-- Castration
-- Beheading.

> What would be acceptable for stalling, cheating [...]

Stalling (when intentional) is a type of cheating. All types of
cheating generally merit severe penalties, such as game loss, of
disqualification. See the link Ira provided.

Note that "slow play" is not considered cheating, since it is not
judged intentional, and generally merits lesser penalties.

> or smoking (when law
> don't prohibit it but organizer asked not to smoke).

Probably covered under the guidelines for "Unsportsmanlike conduct".

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
John Whelan <jwjbw...@gmail.com> wrote:
>On Mar 9, 10:25�am, Satrapa <jedrzej.komorow...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> What are acceptable punishments for misbehavior during tournament?
>
>Acceptable:
>-- A "caution";
>-- A "warning";
>-- A game loss;
>-- A disqualification.

It's also worth bearing in mind that correction of game state is also
possible, which may be perceived by the player as a punishment. The
intention is _not_ to punish - merely to correct for things which have
gone wrong - but this might include things like losing blood, pool, or
other cards/abilities somehow.

(Game state correction obviously doesn't apply where the misbehaviour
isn't related to the game - such as violating a venue's rules on
smoking.)
